content: Sketch the file format for the lake: what goes in the tables and what stays in the media directory
One table for rows, one for tags, one for edges, one for engagements, plus the FTS index; media is hashed and kept next to the file
Why not two files, one for text and one for vectors?
Two files can disagree after a crash. Keeping the vectors in the same file means one lock, one backup, one copy
Fine. Then the design goal is one file per person and nothing else to install
Agreed. I will write that down: one file, no daemon, no required dependencies, and the media directory beside it

I remember the brief settling on SQLite because one file per person is the whole point. Two files can disagree after a crash; one file means one lock, one backup, one copy, and the lake travels as a single thing.
what does the brief say about vectors
The brief leaves them optional: without an embed callback recall is FTS only, and a vector that arrives later is stored in the same file

Q: what does the brief say about vectors
A: they are optional; FTS carries recall without an embed callback, and a vector stored later lands in the same file.

content:
## Where I am
I have spent the last month turning a memory service into a library, and the file is the product now. The server was a host all along; I keep finding that the smaller I make the core, the more of it survives contact with a new host.

## What I keep pulling toward
Provenance that a reader can follow by hand. Every consolidated row cites what it was made from, and I trust the lake more each time that chain holds under a question I did not expect.
Kitchen light on

lake design decisions

Two sessions and a sediment settled the storage format: one file per person, WAL journaling, a five second busy timeout, no required dependencies, provenance kept as a table rather than a tag, and the TTL honoured on every read. The vectors live in the same file so nothing can disagree after a crash.
